page0.text: When I came to, I was lying in a burning field.
page0.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page0:1

page1.text:
It must have been a big fire.
The familiar town was an unrecognizable, smoking ruin. It looked like a scene from a war movie.
The sight didn't last long, though.
As morning dawned, the fires gradually died down.
The towering walls of flame shrunk to embers, and most of the buildings looked to have collapsed.
page1.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page1:1

page2.text:
I was the only one left alive.
I was either fortunate, or the house I'd been inside was built on the luckiest ground of all time.
Either way, I was the only one alive.
page2.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page2:1

page3.text:
Since I'd survived, I felt I needed to keep on living.
I walked aimlessly, thinking it would be dangerous to remain where I was.
It wasn't that I wanted to avoid becoming what had happened to everyone around me...those scorched, blackened masses.
It wasn't a feeling of disgust...
Some other emotion was driving me on.
page3.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page3:1

page4.text:
At the same time, I had no hope.
It was a miracle I was alive at all, and I didn't think I was going to last much longer.
There was just no way in hell I was going to survive.
There was simply no way I would ever escape this crimson hellscape, no matter what I did.
That was how desperate, how hellish this place was, even through the eyes of a young boy.
page4.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page4:1

page5.text:
And then I collapsed.
Either there was no air around me, or I simply couldn't breathe anymore...
I just collapsed. And all I could do was to look up at the slowly clouding sky.
page5.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page5:1

page6.text:
The scorched black masses around me lay motionless.
The dark clouds covered the sky, promising rain.
...Good. The rain will put out the fires.
page6.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page6:1

page7.text:
I took one final deep breath and looked up at the rain clouds.
I couldn't breathe, but I still felt pain.
I said that out loud, on behalf of all those people who couldn't say those words themselves.
page7.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page7:1

page8.text:
That was ten years ago.
Miraculously, in the midst of all that, I was saved.
My physical body survived.
But everything else was scorched... Reduced to ash.
page8.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page8:1

page9.text:
When a young child loses their parents or their home, there's really nothing left of them.
And so, everything other than my body perished.
Put as simply as possible...
In exchange for my body living...
...my heart died.
page9.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page9:1

page10.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page10:1

page11.text:
"...!"
I squinted, seeing a bright white light.
It was blinding.
Light stabbed at my eyes when I woke.
I doubt I really knew what the sensation of blinding light was in the first place.
page11.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page11:1

page12.text:
"Huh...what?"
As my eyes adjusted, I woke, alarmed.
I was lying in a bed I didn't recognize, in a room that I didn't recognize.
I was honestly stunned, but the cleanliness of the white room made me feel at ease.
page12.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page12:1

page13.text:
"...Where am I?"
I looked blankly at my surroundings.
The room was spacious, and beds lined it in neat rows.
All the beds were full, and it looked like each bed's occupant was injured.
page13.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page13:1

page14.text:
But the room didn't feel depressing at all.
Everyone injured survived.
...
I let my eyes wander.
page14.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page14:1

page15.text:
I looked out the window.
The clear blue sky was so incredibly beautiful.
page15.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page15:1

page16.text:
A few days passed, and I was finally able to take in the situation.
I had no problem remembering what happened the days before.
But I wasn't much different from a newborn during this time.
Strange as it is, that was closer to the truth than might seem possible.
page16.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page16:1

page17.text:
The fire was just that bad.
I was rescued from the fire, I awoke in a hospital, my parents were gone, and my entire body was wrapped in bandages.
I didn't really understand what was going on, but I did know that I was alone.
It didn't take long for me to accept my circumstances.
Maybe I had no choice, really; all the other children were in the same boat.
page17.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page17:1

page18.text:
And then, later...
In the moment I, naïve as I was, started to worry about what would become of me, he walked in.
page18.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page18:1

page19.text:
He appeared the day my bandages came off and I started eating on my own.
His hair was disheveled, his suit tattered.
He looked a bit younger than my doctor; he looked more like someone's older brother than someone's father.
page19.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page19:1

page20.text:
"Hello. You must be Shirou."
His beaming smile seemed to blend into the pouring white sunlight.
His voice was somehow irritatingly fake, yet extremely gentle.
page20.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page20:1

page21.text:
"I'll come right to it: Would you rather go to an orphanage, or go home with a man you just met?"
He was offering to take me in.
I asked if we were related. He said we were complete strangers.
He looked like an unremarkable, unreliable guy.
But then again, he was no more or less familiar than the orphanage.
So I decided I'd go with him.
page21.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page21:1

page22.text:
"Oh good. Then let's pack up quickly. It'd be best if you got used to your new home as soon as possible."
He started gathering my things hastily.
Even as young as I was, I could see he wasn't any good at it.
And after he made a mess packing...
page22.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page22:1

page23.text:
"Ah. I forgot to mention one important thing.
Before you come with me, there's one thing you need to know."
He turned, asking for confirmation.
He asked so casually, as if asking me if there was somewhere I wanted to go.
"...Yep.
Let me be direct with you. I'm a magician."
He said it in a serious, almost ceremonious manner.
page23.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page23:1

page24.text:
It happened so fast.
Now that I think back, I was also immature.
I just accepted his words as fact...I took it neither as a joke or genuine statement.
"Really? That's so cool, Pops."
I guess I said something like that, eyes wide in astonishment.
page24.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page24:1

page25.text:
And I was his child.
Actually, I don't really remember how that conversation went.
But every now and then, my old man would bring it up.
He would recount that scene over and over, acting all embarrassed.
That scene might have been the happiest day of my old man—a man named Kiritsugu Emiya's—life.
page25.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page25:1

page26.text:
You can say that...
It was one thing for him to tell a recently orphaned kid he was a magician...
But I was no better, the way I so eagerly bought into it.
And that was how my old man adopted me, and how I took the last name Emiya.
Shirou Emiya.
When I said that name out loud, I felt really proud of having the same last name as Kiritsugu.
page26.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page26:1

page27.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page27:1

page28.text:
It's from my childhood.
It's probably about eight years ago, since it's about the time when I talked my old man into making me his apprentice.
page28.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page28:1

page29.text:
Kiritsugu had started going away on a regular basis once I was old enough to stay home by myself.
He'd always give some childish, unbelievable explanation like, "I'm going to go on an adventure around the world." Then he'd actually do it.
page29.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page29:1

page30.text:
From then on, that's how it always was.
It wasn't unusual for him to be gone for a month, and at times he didn't come home for half a year.
The Emiya mansion is an expansive Japanese samurai-style house, and Kiritsugu and I were the only ones living there.
It felt too big and empty for a child like me, and at times, I felt lost.
page30.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page30:1

page31.text:
But I liked my life there.
Whenever Kiritsugu came home from his trips, he would brag and tell stories like an excited child.
And another child, one who shared his last name, always looked forward to those stories.
I may have been alone in the mansion, but Kiritsugu's stories always helped lessen that.
page31.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page31:1

page32.text:
He was always pursuing a dream like a boy.
I was weary of his whims, yet at the same time he always looked radiant to me.
Maybe that's why I hoped to be like him one day.
page32.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page32:1

page33.text:
Well...
As childish as I might have been, I realized I needed to get my act together, since I had an old man with his head constantly in the clouds.
page33.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page33:1

page34.text:
...I hear a sound.
The heavy, rusted hinges on the door creak as it's being pushed open.
page34.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page34:1

page35.text:
Light pours in through the crack in the door.
"...Hn."
My mind tries to shake off the slumber.
"Senpai, are you awake?"
I hear footsteps drawing near, and I feel the winter air flowing in.
page35.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page35:1

page36.text:
"Hm. Morning, Sakura."
"Yes, good morning to you too, Senpai."
page36.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page36:1

page37.text: "Senpai, it's morning. It's still early, but Ms. Fujimura will be mad if she finds you sleeping here."
page37.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page37:1

page38.text: "Oh...yeah. Thanks for waking me up, as always."
page38.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page38:1

page39.text:
"It is no problem at all. You're always up early in the morning.
I don't often get to wake you up like this."
...?
I'm not sure why, but Sakura looks more cheerful than usual.
page39.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page39:1

page40.text:
"I don't know about that. I think you wake me up more often than you think.
Then again, Fuji-nee is brutal when she's the one waking me up, so I prefer you do it. ...Yep, I've learned my lesson. I'll try not to sleep in here next time."
page40.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page40:1

page41.text:
...I answer, still half-asleep.
My head's still not right, so even I don't know what I'm saying.
page41.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page41:1

page42.text:
"Well, okay. But personally I'd prefer you not to try too hard."
Sakura is giggling.
...Crap. I must still be so sleepy I've said something weird.
page42.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page42:1

page43.text: "Give me a minute to wake up."
page43.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page43:1

page44.text:
The cold winter air helps at times like this.
The chill snaps my lethargic mind awake.
page44.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page44:1

page45.text:
And in front of me stands my junior at school, Sakura Matou.
I'm in my house's storehouse, and it's just about six o'clock in the morning.
page45.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page45:1

page46.text:
"...Senpai?"
"Yeah, I'm awake now. Sorry Sakura, I did it again.
I need to help you with breakfast."
"Don't worry about that. You were up late again last night, weren't you? Then you should take your time this morning. I'll fix breakfast."
page46.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page46:1

page47.text:
Sakura is practically bouncing with excitement.
...That's odd. Sakura is weirdly energetic this morning.
page47.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page47:1

page48.text: "No, no. I'm getting up, honest, so let's head to the kitchen together."
page48.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page48:1

page49.text:
"Okay, I'm ready. Let's go, Sakura."
"Um...well, uh, Senpai."
"Huh? What, is something wrong?"
"No, not exactly...but um...I believe you should change before you head back inside the house."
page49.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page49:1

page50.text:
"Oh..."
I finally look at myself.
I fell asleep working last night, so I'm still wearing my coveralls.
The coveralls I wear while I'm working are usually dirty. Who knows what Fuji-nee would say or do if I went into the house as-is.
page50.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page50:1

page51.text:
"Ugh... Okay, guess I'm not quite awake yet. I must be more out of it than usual."
"You might be right, which is why you should leave breakfast to me, and you should take it easy, Senpai. Besides, Ms. Fujimura would be really angry if she saw the mess here."
page51.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page51:1

page52.text:
"Yeah. Then I'll get changed, so you go on ahead."
"Okay. I'll be waiting, Senpai."
page52.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page52:1

page53.text:
Sakura quickly walks out.
Okay, then...
I'll change into my school uniform first. Then I need to collect all the parts I left scattered around.
page53.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page53:1

page54.text:
The storehouse is in the corner of the backyard, and all sorts of junk is crammed in here.
Though, I've always liked to tinker with gadgets, so the place is a treasure trove to me.
page54.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page54:1

page55.text:
The old man forbade me to go into the storehouse, but I ignored his warnings and snuck inside almost every day. Now it's sort of a base for me.
I guess you could call this place my real room.
The massive Emiya house never felt homey to me, but I've always felt at ease in here, surrounded by all this junk.
page55.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page55:1

page56.text:
"Besides, it's wasteful. It may be junk, but a lot of it still works."
A majority of the things in the storehouse are everyday things, mostly unusable.
page56.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page56:1

page57.text:
I'm not sure whether I brought it all in because I liked it in here, or whether I liked this place because it was full of junk.
Either way, I snuck into this storehouse almost daily, and I made sort of a hobby of fixing broken things.
page57.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page57:1

page58.text:
I'm not the type who gets attached to things.
But it just didn't feel right to neglect things that are still usable...or maybe it would be better to say the idea of doing that just bothered me.
Which is why I stayed up all night trying to fix a broken stove.
page58.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page58:1

page59.text:
"I guess I'll be done tomorrow. Falling asleep midway is proof I'm not concentrating."
I try to shake off my self-disgust at that.
I gather the parts for the stove and put them back on the shelf of things waiting to get fixed.
page59.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page59:1

page60.text:
There's no more room though. Once I fix the stove, an old VCR is up next.
Both of which were destroyed by Fuji-nee. We can set that aside for now...
page60.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page60:1

page61.text:
"Okay, then."
I change into my school uniform.
Since the storehouse is like my own room, I have all the essentials, including changes of clothes, in here.
page61.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page61:1

page62.text:
The rest are things like haphazardly drawn blueprints scattered all over the place and literal junk from my failed attempts at fixing various things.
Also, there's some sort of pattern carved into the storehouse's floor, perhaps used as some sort of an altar in the past.
page62.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page62:1

page63.text:
"Okay. Gotta work hard again today."
I clap my hands in prayer at the storehouse, and turn towards the mansion.
page63.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page63:1

page64.text:
I walk from the storehouse to the mansion.
This Emiya residence is a Japanese samurai-style house, located on the outskirts of town.
My old man wasn't from a notable family, yet for some reason he owned this giant house.
That in itself was a mystery, and it also seems he didn't have any relatives here in Japan.
And so when my old man died, there was no one else to inherit this mansion, so it came to me as his adopted son.
page64.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page64:1

page65.text:
Though to be honest, I don't have any administrative abilities.
So things like inheritance, property taxes, and any other complicated things are all handled by Old Man Fujimura.
page65.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page65:1

page66.text:
Old Man Fujimura is a major businessman who lives nearby.
Kiritsugu described Old Man Fujimura as an old man who's "like a yakuza boss."
Obviously, that was his own biased view.
In fact, Old Man Fujimura is not like a yakuza boss, he is a yakuza boss.
page66.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page66:1

page67.text:
"..."
That may be a problem in itself, but I try not to dwell on it.
page67.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page67:1

page69.text:
Anyway, that's why I live in this giant mansion on my own.
It's been five years since my old man died.
Time sure does fly.
I sigh, thinking about how much I've grown in those five years.
page69.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page69:1

page70.text:
I trained every day to become like Kiritsugu, but that's easier said than done.
It's not surprising, since I didn't have what it takes from the start. But the fact that I haven't improved at all these past five years forces me to reassess things.
If I had to sum up my current situation, I'd say I set the bar too high. I haven't even reached the starting line.
page70.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page70:1

page71.text:
"..."
No, rushing won't do me any good.
For now, I just have to do what I can.
page71.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page71:1

page72.text:
Okay, then.
What I need to do now is—
page72.sourceUnit: セイバールート一日目-00:page72:1
